t.10.1: The Blessed Lord said: Once again, O mighty-armed one, hear my supreme word, which I shall speak to you, who take delight in it, out of a wish for your welfare.
t.10.2: Neither the hosts of gods nor the great sages know my origin, for I am in every way the source of the gods and of the great sages.
t.10.3: He who knows me as unborn and without beginning, the great Lord of the worlds, he among mortals is undeluded and is freed from all sins.
t.10.4: Intelligence, knowledge, freedom from delusion, forbearance, truthfulness, self-restraint and tranquility, pleasure and pain, birth and non-existence, fear and also fearlessness,
t.10.5: Non-violence, equanimity, contentment, austerity, charity, fame and infamy: these various states of beings arise from me alone.
t.10.7: He who truly knows this manifold glory and this yoga of mine is united with unwavering yoga; of this there is no doubt.
t.10.6: The seven great sages of old, and likewise the four Manus, sharing my nature, were born from my mind, and from them have come these creatures in the world.
t.10.8: I am the origin of all; from me everything proceeds. Understanding this, the wise, filled with devotion, worship me.
t.10.9: With their minds fixed on Me, their lives devoted to Me, enlightening one another and constantly speaking of Me, they are content and they rejoice.
t.10.10: To those who are ever devoted and worship Me with love, I give that yoga of understanding by which they come to Me.
t.10.11: Out of compassion for them alone, I, dwelling within their very being, destroy the darkness born of ignorance with the shining lamp of knowledge.
t.10.12: Arjuna said: You are the supreme Brahman, the supreme abode, the supreme purifier; you are the one they proclaim as the eternal divine Person, the primal God, unborn and all-pervading.
t.10.13: All the seers have declared this of you, and so has the divine seer Nārada, as well as Asita, Devala and Vyāsa; and you yourself tell me so.
t.10.14: All this that you tell me, O Keśava, I hold to be true. For neither the gods nor the Dānavas know your manifestation, O Blessed Lord.
t.10.16: You ought to describe completely your own divine manifestations, the manifestations by which you pervade these worlds and abide.
t.10.15: You yourself alone know yourself through yourself, O Supreme Person, O source of beings, O lord of beings, O god of gods, O lord of the world.
t.10.17: How may I know you, O Yogin, while constantly meditating upon you? And in what various states of being are you to be contemplated by me, O Bhagavan?
t.10.18: Tell me again in detail, O Janārdana, of your yoga and your divine manifestations, for as I listen to this nectar, I am never satisfied.
t.10.19: The Blessed Lord said: Very well, I shall tell you of My divine self-manifestations, O best of the Kurus, but only the principal ones, for there is no end to My extent.
t.10.20: I am the Self, O Guḍākeśa, abiding in the heart of all beings. I am the beginning, the middle, and also the very end of beings.
t.10.21: Of the Ādityas I am Viṣṇu; of lights I am the radiant sun. Of the Maruts I am Marīci; among the stars I am the moon.
t.10.22: Of the Vedas I am the Sāmaveda; of the gods I am Vāsava; of the senses I am the mind; and of living beings I am consciousness.
t.10.23: Among the Rudras I am Śaṃkara, and among the Yakṣas and Rākṣasas I am Vitteśa, the lord of wealth. Among the Vasus I am Pāvaka, and among the peaked mountains I am Meru.
t.10.24: Know me, O Pārtha, as Bṛhaspati, the chief among the household priests; among army leaders I am Skanda, and among bodies of water I am the ocean.
t.10.25: Among the great sages I am Bhṛgu; among utterances I am the single syllable. Among sacrifices I am the sacrifice of japa, and among immovable things I am the Himālaya.
t.10.26: Among all trees I am the Aśvattha, and among the divine sages I am Nārada; among the Gandharvas I am Citraratha, and among the perfected ones I am the sage Kapila.
t.10.27: Among horses, know me to be Uccaiḥśravas, born of the nectar of immortality; among lordly elephants, Airāvata; and among men, the king.
t.10.28: Among weapons I am the thunderbolt, among cows I am Kāmadhuk, the wish-fulfilling cow; of progenitors I am Kandarpa, and among serpents I am Vāsuki.
t.10.29: Of the Nāgas I am Ananta, and of the water-dwellers I am Varuṇa; of the ancestors I am Aryaman, and of those who restrain I am Yama.
t.10.30: Among the Daityas I am Prahlāda, and among those who reckon I am Time; among beasts I am the lord of beasts, and among birds I am Vainateya.
t.10.31: Of purifiers I am the wind; of the wielders of weapons I am Rāma. Of fishes I am the makara, and of rivers I am the Jāhnavī.
t.10.32: Of creations I am the beginning and the end, and also the middle, O Arjuna; of sciences I am the science of the Self, and of those who debate I am the reasoned discourse.
t.10.33: Of letters I am the letter A, and of compounds I am the dvaṃdva. I alone am imperishable Time; I am the Sustainer, facing in all directions.
t.10.34: I am all-devouring Death, and I am the origin of all that is yet to be. Among feminine things, I am fame, prosperity, speech, memory, intelligence, steadfastness and forgiveness.
t.10.35: Likewise, of the Sāman hymns I am the Bṛhatsāman; of the metres I am the Gāyatrī. Of the months I am Mārgaśīrṣa; of the seasons I am the flower-bearing spring.
t.10.36: Of those who deceive, I am the gambling; I am the splendor of the splendid. I am victory, I am resolve, I am the goodness of the good.
t.10.37: Of the Vṛṣṇis I am Vāsudeva; of the Pāṇḍavas, Dhanaṃjaya; of the sages I am Vyāsa; and of the seers, the seer Uśanas.
t.10.40: There is no end to my divine manifestations, O scorcher of foes. But this extent of my glory has been declared by me only by way of example.
t.10.38: Of those who subdue, I am the rod of punishment; of those who seek victory, I am statecraft. Of secret things I am silence, and of the wise I am wisdom.
t.10.41: Whatever being there is that is endowed with glory, splendid, or mighty, know that very thing to have sprung from a portion of my radiance.
t.10.42: But what need is there for you, Arjuna, to know all this in such detail? I stand, supporting this entire universe with a single fraction of Myself.
t.10.39: And whatever is the seed of all beings, that am I, O Arjuna; there is no being, moving or unmoving, that could exist without me.
